packages.title: REPD National Data Library project-stage QA
facts: The National Data Library describes REPD as tracking renewable projects from planning application through consent, construction and operation.
The dataset was updated in July 2026.
Project-stage data are administrative/project-development evidence.
Project-stage evidence does not establish realised renewable generation or avoided emissions.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: REPD planning record versus avoided-GHG QA
facts: A renewable project can appear in REPD before operation.
Planning progress must not be converted into assumed annual generation.
Without generation and counterfactual evidence, avoided greenhouse-gas emissions cannot be established from planning status alone.
Site-area or capacity fields also require separate performance assumptions.
No avoided parcel emissions are fabricated.

packages.title: Heat Networks Planning Database project-stage QA
facts: HNPD covers district and communal heat-network deployment across the UK.
It tracks stages including inception, planning, construction, operation and decommissioning.
Data are assembled from planning applications and developer contact.
Project stage is not the same as heat delivered or emissions avoided.
No parcel greenhouse-gas value is inferred.

packages.title: Heat Networks Planning Database update-lag QA
facts: HNPD is updated during the month following the end of each quarter.
The current dataset includes a defined reporting window and project-pipeline status.
Quarterly update timing creates a normal publication lag.
Pipeline records should not be treated as real-time operating measurements.
No site emissions value is inferred from update timing.

packages.title: Energy Trends renewables scope QA
facts: Energy Trends renewables tables cover renewable electricity capacity and generation.
They also include liquid-biofuel consumption information.
The renewables page was updated on 9 July 2026 with the June 2026 Energy Trends release.
Capacity, generation and fuel consumption are different energy measures.
None should be relabelled as a parcel greenhouse-gas measurement.

packages.title: Renewable capacity versus generation QA
facts: Renewable capacity is a power-system stock measure.
Renewable electricity generation is an energy-flow measure.
Liquid biofuel consumption is another distinct activity measure.
These measures can inform emissions analysis only with appropriate boundaries and factors.
No parcel emissions quantity is inferred directly.

packages.title: ONS Environmental Accounts fossil-fuel table scope QA
facts: ONS Environmental Accounts provide fuel-use data by fuel type from 1990 to 2024.
The fossil-fuel table includes fuels such as coal, natural gas, petrol, DERV, fuel oil, gas oil and aviation fuel.
The stated fossil-fuel table excludes biofuels and waste.
Fuel use is an activity/energy measure and is distinct from greenhouse-gas emissions.
No parcel emission value is inferred from national fuel use.

packages.title: ONS reallocated energy by industry QA
facts: ONS publishes total direct energy use including fossil fuels and other sources.
It also publishes reallocated energy use and energy intensity by industry.
Industry reallocation changes the accounting view of energy use and must retain its methodology.
Energy intensity is not the same as absolute greenhouse-gas emissions.
No property-level emissions estimate is created.

packages.title: Landfill methane measurement difficulty QA
facts: Environment Agency research identifies landfill methane as an important greenhouse-gas source from decomposing organic waste.
Landfill-gas collection is mandatory in England for permitted landfills accepting biodegradable wastes.
Residual methane emissions can arise from multiple sources across a wide area.
The report notes that measuring residual landfill methane is difficult.
No landfill parcel emission is inferred without site-specific measurement evidence.

packages.title: Landfill methane measurement-method research QA
facts: The research examined two measurement approaches for landfill methane.
It considered how measurements could be used in regulation.
The work found measurement could help improve landfill-gas capture and reduce methane emissions.
A research-method assessment is not itself a measured emission for every landfill.
No site value is fabricated.

packages.title: England household waste 2024 tonnage QA
facts: England's 2024 waste-from-households recycling rate was 43.8%.
Total waste from households was about 21.9 million tonnes.
About 9.6 million tonnes were sent for recycling and 12.3 million tonnes were residual waste.
Waste tonnage and recycling rates are activity statistics, not greenhouse-gas emissions.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from waste tonnage.

packages.title: Local-authority waste treatment 2024/25 QA
facts: Total local-authority-managed waste in 2024/25 was about 25.2 million tonnes.
About 1.4 million tonnes, or 5.5%, were sent to landfill.
About 12.7 million tonnes, or 50.3%, were sent to incineration.
Treatment tonnage does not by itself establish methane, CO2 or CO2e emissions.
No property-level waste emissions are calculated.

packages.title: Fly-tipping 2024/25 incident count QA
facts: Local authorities in England dealt with about 1.26 million fly-tipping incidents in 2024/25.
The total was reported as 9% higher than in 2023/24.
Household waste was involved in 62% of recorded incidents, around 777,000 incidents.
Incident counts are enforcement/waste-management statistics rather than greenhouse-gas measurements.
No parcel emission value is inferred from an incident count.

packages.title: Fly-tipping coverage and methodology guard QA
facts: The local-authority fly-tipping statistics exclude the large-scale incidents dealt with by the Environment Agency and most private-land incidents.
The publication notes a methodology change affecting comparability from 2019/20.
Coverage and methodology must be preserved in time-series comparisons.
Fly-tipping presence does not determine the mass or emissions profile of waste.
No property greenhouse-gas quantity is inferred.

packages.title: UK PRTR facility and environmental-media QA
facts: UK PRTR data cover industrial facilities and their geographical locations.
They report pollutant releases to environmental media including air, water and land.
They also cover off-site transfers of waste and pollutants in wastewater.
PRTR reporting is facility-based and threshold-based.
A facility report is not automatically a cadastral parcel emission value.

packages.title: UK PRTR measured calculated estimated method-code QA
facts: PRTR operator data can be reported as calculated, estimated, measured or unspecified.
The guidance lists method sub-categories for calculation and measurement approaches.
Operator submissions are subject to quality checks using permits, inspections and monitoring information.
Method code must be preserved when interpreting a reported release.
No calculated or estimated facility value is relabelled as a direct parcel measurement.
